slides.heading: Simple Calculations
slides.body: Simple Calculations is part of Mathematical and String Operations. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: Simple Calculations
slides.body: Simple calculations combine operators, variables, and output. They help build programs for totals, averages, and conversions.

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: A calculation program is like a small cashier calculator that follows the same formula every time.

slides.heading: Key Rule
slides.body: Python follows operator rules exactly. Use variables and parentheses to make calculations readable and predictable.

slides.heading: Try It Yourself!
slides.prompt: Calculate the total of two scores and print it.
slides.hint: Add the two variables inside print() or store the result first.

coding_challenge.prompt_text: Compute the average of 80 and 90 and print it.
coding_challenge.hint_text: Use the idea from the lesson. Keep the code short, readable, and correctly indented.
